about: What a .tidegraph holds (notes/visual-scripting.md): every kind of declaration, member and node, the keys of each in the order tidec writes them, and a node's ports. tidec reads it for its own nodes' inputs; tidels serves it to graph editors (tide/graphSchema).

rules: An input takes one wire; wiring another replaces it.
A statement runs from one place: an exec output takes one wire, and a statement is wired from one exec output.
No value is made of itself: a data wire can't close a loop.
A value wired to two inputs is worked out at each.
A local is read where what declares it has run.
A simple value is in the input that reads it: a number, text, a name, a path of fields. A value worked out by a call or an operator is a node wired in.

inline.about: A value read by one input is shown in that input, edited there, and is no node of its own: a literal or a name (always), a member of what is itself shown there (path: ball.position.x), a '-' over a number (negative), a vector or a colour made of numbers alone (numbers: a call named one of numbersOf whose arguments are all numbers, float2(16, 14)). Everything else is a node wired in. tidec's layout gives them no room (graph_layout_fold).
